title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises to adopt new business models, technology and techniques to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative: By 2021, more than 13, 000 existing and potential entrepreneurs in Myanmar had been trained in ILO's Start & Improve Your Business (SIYB) training programm. A robust network of more than 700 certified trainers and a core team of master trainers and a formally registered association/non-profit entity were also established to provide trainings to entrepreneurs, coordinate and support training delivery throughout the country.The private sector freelance trainers and training companies embedded SCORE Training in their programmes. By June 2021, Trainers had trained 159 enterprises in SCORE, which employ 3,571 staff members, and ii) developed a core team of 33 certified SCORE trainers. As an institutional platform established for delivering business development services (BDS), the SIYB Association Myanmar serves as a formal organization to provide capacity-strengthening support to trainers, enable them to access opportunities for serving BDS to clients, and promoting entrepreneurship through public events. Based on SIYB Global e-guidelines, SIYB Myanmar Association adapted the general e-training guidelines and examples in designing initial simplified online training products in Myanmar. It also developed a set of trainers' guides and e-M&E tools in December 2020 and conducted TOTs for these online training packages in February 2021. Three complementary entities including SIYB Myanmar Association were identified to further ensure sustainability of the BDS platform. Through interventions promoting the development of target value chains (Asian seabass and tourism), the United KMK hatchery, in July 2020, completed their 2nd batch of Asian seabass fingerlings, which brings the annual total 84% higher than baseline year of 2018. The lead farmers also managed the sale of 12 metric tonnes of Asian seabass to 2 Yangon processing factories in 2020, with a sales price above normal market rates and without commission which is required to sell through regular traders. In 2020-2021, the ILO expanded activities to support the development of MSMEs throughout Myanmar with support from Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation (NORAD) and the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO). This included provision of the ILO's Start & Improve Your Business (SIYB) training programme, which includes Generate Your Business Idea, Start Your Business and Improve Your Business. The ILO also expanded the network of trainers for Sustaining Competitive and Responsible Enterprises (SCORE) to improve productivity and working conditions in SMEs through better workplace cooperation. The ILO supported the SIYB Myanmar Association to improve its capacity for Business Development Services (BDS) marketing through organizing partnership-brokering sessions for the association to secure external resources for further product development and delivery of training services. To further ensure sustainability of the BDS platform, the ILO organized series of consultation meetings with implementing partners leading to the conceptualization of three complementary entities which includes the SYIB Myanmar Association, formal/informal networks/consortia of individual trainers, and individual freelance trainers. Besides training interventions, the ILO also provided technical and operational support to priority value chains which have high potential to benefit MSMEs, in 2020-2021, Asian seabass and tourism value chains was focused. In the seabass value chain, the ILO supported the United KMK hatchery with on-site consulting, together with overseas study and training visits to commercial hatcheries and government facilities in Indonesia, and development of a Standard Operating Procedure, which provides reference tools to summarise and standardise planning and implementation of the new production methods. In 2020, the ILO organized meetings to link farmers directly to processing factories in Yangon, as an alternative to selling through a chain of traders.

Output 3.4. Increased capacity of ILO constituents to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

description.narrative:
In 2020, Ethnic Armed Organizations (EAOs) and their communities in Mon and Kayin States agreed to adopt labour based technologies as a way forward to rebuild their communities in term of basic infrastructures post ceasefire. Other forms of employment also stemmed from there after basic infrastructures were in place (such as trading of agriculture products, market place creation after footpath and small roads for transportation of goods). In mid-2020, EAOs and ethnic communities started to discuss with government local authorities on how to work together on skill development, and job creation opportunities. The communities affected by conflict and the COVID-19 crisis gradually detached themselves from being dependent on support from humanitarian actors and started to sustain their own livelihoods with strengthened employability. In Rakhine State, the first Skills Assessment Centre accredited by National Skills Standards Authority was established involving private sector, Department of Labour, and other ministries to improve access to skills assessment capacities and employability in Rakhine. In February 2020, the State government launched the first-ever Rakhine State Skills Development Technical Working Group established with representatives from private sector, employers, workers and other actors in skills development and job creation to strengthen the skills development of workers to address the requirements of local and foreign companies willing to invest in Rakhine State. In 2020, newly formed 20 village development committees in central and southern parts of Rakhine developed and implemented their livelihood projects based on the local needs and opportunities. Through avenues for intercommunal trust building provided with establishment of a shared space for work and commerce, the intercommunal activities with positive interaction took place among the diverse ethnic groups of people (Hindus,Rakhine and Muslim) in northern Rakhine. In 2020-2021, the ILO with the support of New Zealand Government, undertook activities with labour intensive technology in conflict-affected Mon and Kayin States where level of human rights and labour rights violation was more severe than in other parts of the country. Through proper due diligence process, ILO identified local implementing partners under framework of conflict sensitivity and do no harm principle. The ILO provided the short-term employment through cash for work programmes in construction of WASH facilities and other essential small-scale public infrastructure in poor, remittance dependent, communities. For medium term, the ILO also provided short TVET courses and non-certified livelihoods and construction training delivered that increase skills and employability of people in remittance dependent communities for domestic and migrant work.
In 2020, the ILO with support of Livelihoods and Food Security Fund (LIFT) continued to strengthen the technical and vocational education training system and structures in Rakhine State. This includes establishment of the ever first government-accredited skills assessment centre in region, and formation of Skill Development Technical working group where ILO assumed secretariat role to provide technical support to Department of Labour and partners to ensure easily accessible skill development and employment. The ILO pivoted its approach in expanding its coverage of technical vocational skills development beyond formal learning structures and towards directly engaging with communities through village development committees. It was a deliberate push to establish "safe and shared work spaces" for community cohesion among diverse ethnic groups of people in Rakhine. Community based enterprises focusing on intercommunal shared service facilities demonstrated that between and among the skills training completers who are Hindus, Rakhine and Muslim, some degree of positive interactions takes place.
